scope: Identify why joint proposals fail final strict geometry checks without weakening those checks
retained_change: Diagnostic mode reports the first failed physical separation, axis and actual forward-sum values. It uses the already required comparisons; no additional solver/geometry work or acceptance-policy change.

baseline_diagnostic.initial_checks: Placement and flow PASS, hard RED 0; same geometry and event count as previous candidate

rejected_experiment.strategy: Add 0.0001 mm (one final 4-decimal output step) to movable/movable joint-search separation gaps. Keep unmodified required separations for final physical checks. Fixed obstacles, hard terms, final collision/flow gates unchanged.
rejected_experiment.result: Constructed 165x159, placement and flow PASS, hard RED 0. Joint proposals 121 -> 10 and qualification rejections 116 -> 0, but this is a different search path and layout, not a same-output timing comparison.
reasons: Increased successful reseats beyond the committed ceiling
Unconditional guard can exclude tightly fitting candidates; an incumbent-preserving strategy is needed
Different PCB not independently fully qualified; no new accepted carrier
rejected_experiment.restoration: Guarded domain and alternate required-separation storage removed; normal search rebuilt

regression_test.witness: Two movable groups: 0.1 + 0.1 + 0.1 > 0.3 in binary floating point; a satisfiable near term activates legalization. Diagnostic and non-diagnostic modes both reject the strict physical contact, preserve input poses and produce equal operation counts. Only diagnostic mode reports the exact boundary.

acceptance: No new accepted layout, hardware-policy change or raised execution ceiling. Existing 165x159 candidate still fails execution ratchet; qualified 166x159 remains the incumbent.
next: Implement narrowly bounded, accounted grid-safe repair that preserves unmodified requirements and feasible incumbents; avoid globally inflating gaps or relaxing collision tolerances. Preserve actual numerical values in failure evidence.
